headline: UK economy grew faster than first thought in the second quarter

terms.meaning: The total value of goods and services an economy produces.
A group of seven large advanced economies.
Money firms spend on things like machinery and buildings.

levels.headline: UK economy grew faster than first thought in the second quarter
levels.body:
Britain's economy grew by 0.5% in the second quarter of 2026, the April to June period, a stronger result than first estimated. Output was 1.4% higher than a year earlier, according to the revised figures, which were reported as cementing the UK's lead among G7 economies.
Business investment was also revised up, to an annual rate of 5.2%. GDP per head, which measures output per person and so strips out the effect of population growth, rose by 1.1% over the first half of 2026. That was reported as the largest increase since late 2017, leaving aside the swings caused by the pandemic.
The picture ahead is less certain. Commentators such as PwC have pointed to uncertainty over the Budget and a sustained rise in energy prices as the weather turns colder as risks to growth.
The figures matter because growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has available to spend.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: UK growth revised up for the second quarter, keeping Britain ahead in the G7
levels.body:
The UK economy expanded by 0.5% between April and June 2026, more than first estimated, and was 1.4% larger than a year earlier. The revision was reported as cementing Britain's lead among G7 economies.
Business investment was revised up to a 5.2% annual rate. GDP per head, a measure of output per person, grew by 1.1% in the first half of 2026, the biggest rise since late 2017 once the pandemic's distortions are set aside.
Looking forward, PwC has flagged Budget uncertainty and rising energy prices as winter approaches as risks to the recovery.
Growth matters because it influences employment, pay and how much room the government has for tax and spending decisions.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: UK economy grew 0.5% in the spring, more than first thought
levels.body:
Britain's economy grew by 0.5% between April and June 2026, after revised figures showed it did better than first estimated. It was 1.4% bigger than a year before, and the result was reported as keeping the UK ahead of other G7 economies.
Business investment was revised up to an annual rate of 5.2%. Output per person, known as GDP per head, rose 1.1% in the first half of the year, the largest increase since late 2017 apart from pandemic swings.
There are worries about what comes next. PwC has pointed to uncertainty about the Budget and to energy prices rising as the weather gets colder.
Stronger growth can help create jobs and raise wages, and it gives the government more money from taxes to spend.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: Britain's economy did better than expected this spring
levels.body:
Britain's economy grew by 0.5% between April and June 2026. That is more than experts first thought. It was also 1.4% bigger than a year earlier. Reports said this keeps the UK ahead of the other G7 countries, a group of large rich economies.
Money spent by firms on things like machines and buildings, called business investment, was also revised up. GDP per head, which means the amount the economy produces for each person, rose 1.1% in the first half of the year. That is the biggest rise since late 2017, not counting the odd years of the pandemic.
There are some worries about the months ahead. PwC, a firm of experts, pointed to uncertainty over the Budget and to energy prices going up as it gets colder.
A growing economy can mean more jobs and better pay for people.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: UK economy grew 0.5% in spring, more than first estimated
levels.body:
Britain's economy grew by 0.5% between April and June 2026, after revised figures showed it had done better than first thought. It was 1.4% bigger than a year earlier, and reports said this keeps the UK ahead of other G7 economies, the group of large rich countries.
Companies also invested more in things like machinery and buildings, at an annual rate of 5.2%. The amount produced for each person, called GDP per head, rose 1.1% in the first half of the year, the biggest rise since late 2017 apart from pandemic swings.
There are risks ahead. PwC has pointed to doubts about the Budget, the government's plan for tax and spending, and to energy prices rising as the weather turns colder.
Stronger growth can mean more jobs and better pay, and it brings the government more money from taxes.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: The UK economy grew more than people thought
levels.body:
The UK economy grew by 0.5% between April and June 2026. When experts looked again at the numbers, they found it had done better than they first said. It was also 1.4% bigger than a year before. News reports said the UK is doing better than the other G7 countries, which are seven big rich countries.
Firms also spent more on machines and buildings than first thought. The amount of goods and services made for each person went up by 1.1% in the first half of the year. That is the biggest rise since late 2017, apart from the strange pandemic years.
Experts at PwC say there are some risks ahead. People do not yet know what will be in the Budget, and energy prices are rising as winter comes.
When the economy grows, it can mean more jobs and higher pay.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: The UK made more than expected this spring
levels.body:
The UK economy grew by 0.5% between April and June 2026. The economy is all the things a country makes and sells, like food, cars and services. Experts looked at the numbers again and found it had grown more than they thought. It was 1.4% bigger than a year before.
Reports said this is better than the other G7 countries, which are seven big rich countries. Firms also spent more on machines and buildings. The amount made for each person went up by 1.1% in the first half of the year, the most since late 2017, not counting the pandemic years.
Some experts are still careful. They say people do not know yet what the government will do in the Budget, and that energy costs are going up as it gets cold.
A growing economy can mean more jobs and more pay.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: The country made more than expected
levels.body:
The UK economy grew between April and June this year. An economy is everything a country makes and sells, like food, cars and help from doctors. It grew by 0.5% in those three months. Experts first thought it grew less.
Over a whole year it grew 1.4%. News reports said this beats other rich countries in a group called the G7. Companies also spent more money on machines and buildings. And each person in the UK, on average, was part of 1.1% more being made in the first half of the year.
Experts also said to be careful. The government will soon explain its plans for taxes and spending, called the Budget, and no one knows yet what it will say. Heating and energy are also getting dearer as winter comes.
When a country makes more, there can be more jobs and more pay.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: The country got a bit richer this spring
levels.body:
Think of the whole country as a big shop. Between April and June, the shop sold more than people expected. It sold 0.5% more than before. That is a small step up, like adding one extra sweet to every two hundred.
Over a whole year, it sold 1.4% more. Reports said this is better than other rich countries. Shops and firms also spent more on machines and buildings. Each person in the country, on average, was part of a little more being made.
Grown-ups say we should be careful. A big plan about taxes and spending, called the Budget, is coming and nobody knows what is in it. Keeping warm is also getting dearer as winter comes.
When the shop does well, more people can have jobs and bigger pay.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

levels.headline: How the country did this spring
levels.body:
Each year, grown-ups count how much the whole country makes and sells. Between April and June, it was a bit more than they first thought. It went up by half of one in every hundred. That is a small step, like a plant growing a tiny bit taller.
Over a whole year, the country made 1.4% more. Reports said that is better than other rich countries. Firms also spent more on machines and buildings.
Some grown-ups are still careful. A plan about money, called the Budget, is coming soon. Heating is also getting dearer as the weather gets colder.
When a country grows, more people can get jobs and be paid more. That is why grown-ups watch these numbers.
levels.why: Growth affects jobs, wages and the money the government has to spend.

headline: Andy Burnham settles into Downing Street as Labour tensions surface

terms.meaning: The group of senior ministers who lead the government.
A rule that raises the state pension each year by the highest of inflation, wage growth or 2.5%.

levels.headline: Andy Burnham settles into Downing Street as Labour tensions surface
levels.body:
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned, making him Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade. He had stood down as Mayor of Greater Manchester in June and entered Parliament as MP for Makerfield that same month.
Rachel Reeves left government in July, saying she would support Burnham's Labour government. Early October reports described a cabinet revolt over a proposed overhaul of the voting system, and calls from Labour MPs to scrap the family farm tax. Commentators also warned about a reported plan to scrap the pension triple lock, which guarantees yearly rises in the state pension.
The Conservatives, led by Kemi Badenoch, held their annual party conference in early October.
The first months of a new prime minister shape how much support a government keeps, both in Parliament and with voters.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: Burnham's government faces early divisions over policy
levels.body:
Andy Burnham has been Prime Minister since July 2026, when Keir Starmer resigned. Burnham is the seventh prime minister in a decade. He left his role as Mayor of Greater Manchester in June and became MP for Makerfield that month.
Rachel Reeves left government in July and said she would back the new Labour government. Reports in early October described a cabinet revolt over a voting system overhaul, and Labour MPs calling for the family farm tax to be scrapped. Commentators also raised concerns about a reported plan to end the triple lock on pensions.
Meanwhile the Conservatives, under Kemi Badenoch, prepared for their annual conference in early October.
A new leader's early decisions affect party unity and public trust.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: Burnham's first months as Prime Minister
levels.body:
Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned, the seventh prime minister in ten years. He had quit as Mayor of Greater Manchester in June and won a seat in Parliament as MP for Makerfield.
Chancellor Rachel Reeves left the government in July but said she would support Burnham. In early October, reports spoke of a cabinet revolt over changes to the voting system and of Labour MPs wanting the family farm tax dropped. Commentators warned about a reported plan to scrap the pension triple lock.
The Conservatives, led by Kemi Badenoch, were getting ready for their annual conference.
How a new prime minister handles disputes in their own party can decide how long they last.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: Andy Burnham is Prime Minister, but his party is not all agreed
levels.body:
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned. He is the seventh prime minister the UK has had in ten years. Before that he was Mayor of Greater Manchester, and he became an MP in June.
Rachel Reeves left the government in July. She said she would still support the new Labour government. In early October, news reports described a row in the cabinet, the group of senior ministers, about changing how people vote. Some Labour MPs also want the family farm tax scrapped. There is also talk of ending the triple lock, a rule that makes the state pension rise every year.
The Conservative Party, led by Kemi Badenoch, was getting ready for its yearly conference.
If a governing party argues in public, it can find it harder to pass laws.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: Andy Burnham is Prime Minister but Labour is not united
levels.body:
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned. He is the seventh prime minister in ten years. He had been Mayor of Greater Manchester and became MP for Makerfield in June.
Rachel Reeves left the government in July but said she would back it. In early October, reports described a row among senior ministers over changing the voting system, and Labour MPs asking for the family farm tax to be scrapped. There was also concern over a reported plan to end the triple lock, which makes the state pension rise each year.
The Conservatives, led by Kemi Badenoch, held their yearly conference.
When a governing party argues in public, it can find it harder to pass its plans.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: A new Prime Minister faces arguments in his own party
levels.body:
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026, after Keir Starmer stepped down. He is the seventh person to hold the job in ten years. Before this he was the Mayor of Greater Manchester, and he joined Parliament as an MP in June.
Rachel Reeves left the government in July but said she still backs it. In early October, reports said senior ministers were arguing about changing the voting system. Some Labour MPs also want a tax on family farms to be dropped. People are also talking about a reported plan to end the triple lock, which makes the state pension go up each year.
The Conservatives, led by Kemi Badenoch, held their yearly conference.
When a party in government disagrees with itself, it can be harder to get plans done.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: The UK has a new Prime Minister and some disagreements
levels.body:
Andy Burnham became the UK's Prime Minister in July 2026. The last one, Keir Starmer, stepped down. The UK has now had seven prime ministers in ten years. Mr Burnham used to be the Mayor of Greater Manchester. In June he became an MP, which is a person chosen to speak for an area in Parliament.
Rachel Reeves, who had looked after the country's money, left the government in July. She said she still supports it. In October, reports said some top ministers were arguing about changing how people vote. Some MPs want a tax on family farms to be dropped. There is also talk of ending the triple lock, a rule that makes the state pension go up every year.
The Conservative Party, led by Kemi Badenoch, was getting ready for its yearly meeting.
A government that argues a lot can find it harder to get things done.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: A new leader and some arguments
levels.body:
The UK has a new Prime Minister. His name is Andy Burnham. He took over in July 2026 when the last one, Keir Starmer, stepped down. The Prime Minister is the person who leads the government. The UK has had seven in ten years, which is a lot.
Mr Burnham was a mayor in Manchester before this. Then he became an MP, a person who speaks for an area in Parliament. In October, news reports said some of his top team were arguing about changing how people vote. Some MPs also want a tax on family farms to stop. People are also talking about the triple lock, a rule that makes the state pension go up every year.
Another party, the Conservatives, led by Kemi Badenoch, held its yearly meeting.
When a team argues, it is harder for it to get anything done.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: A new leader for the country
levels.body:
The UK has a new Prime Minister called Andy Burnham. A Prime Minister is the person in charge of the government, like a head teacher for the whole country. He started in July 2026 when the last one, Keir Starmer, stepped down.
Before this, Mr Burnham was a mayor in Manchester. He then became an MP, a person chosen to speak for their area. In October, reports said some of his team did not agree about some plans. They were arguing about how people vote, and about a tax on farms.
Another group of politicians, the Conservatives, held their yearly meeting too. Their leader is Kemi Badenoch.
When people on the same team do not agree, it is harder to get a plan done.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

levels.headline: Who is in charge of the country
levels.body:
Every country needs someone in charge. In the UK, that person is called the Prime Minister. In July, a man called Andy Burnham got the job. The last one, Keir Starmer, stepped down. It is a bit like a new captain of a football team.
Mr Burnham used to be a mayor in Manchester. His team is called the Labour party. In October, grown-ups said some people in his team did not agree about some plans. It is like when friends in a team argue about the rules of a game.
Another team of politicians, called the Conservatives, also had a big yearly meeting.
When a team argues a lot, it is harder for them to win the game together.
levels.why: A new prime minister's early decisions shape party unity and public trust.

headline: Oil climbs as record tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz cut shipping

terms.meaning: The main international benchmark price for oil.
A narrow waterway between Iran and Oman used to ship much of the world's oil.

levels.headline: Oil climbs as record tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz cut shipping
levels.body:
Oil prices jumped on Thursday 8 October after a record number of attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude, the main international benchmark, rose 4% to close at $104.28 a barrel. Crossings of the strait fell to a two-month low.
The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which a large share of the world's oil is shipped, so any threat to ships there quickly feeds into prices. Reports blamed Iran for stepping up the attacks.
A separate supply worry came from the US Gulf of Mexico, where a hurricane led oil companies to shut in about 500,000 barrels a day, roughly 25% of production in the area. Prices came off their highs after President Donald Trump said the United States would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections.
Higher oil prices tend to push up fuel and transport costs, which can raise inflation and complicate the work of central banks.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil rises as tanker attacks near Hormuz hit a record
levels.body:
Oil prices rose sharply on Thursday 8 October after a record number of attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude, the global benchmark, gained 4% to close at $104.28 a barrel, and ship crossings of the strait dropped to a two-month low.
The strait, which lies between Iran and Oman, is one of the most important routes for the world's oil. Reports said Iran had stepped up its attacks on vessels there, which made traders worry about supply.
Another pressure came from the US Gulf of Mexico, where companies shut in around 500,000 barrels a day, about a quarter of output in the area, because of a hurricane. Prices eased from their peaks after President Trump said America would not attack Iran before November's midterm elections.
Because oil feeds into petrol, diesel and freight costs, a sustained rise can add to inflation and affect interest rate decisions.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Brent crude jumps 4% after record number of tanker attacks
levels.body:
Brent crude rose 4% on Thursday 8 October to close at $104.28 a barrel, as a record number of attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz raised fears about oil supplies. Crossings through the strait fell to a two-month low.
The strait, between Iran and Oman, is a key shipping route for oil, and reports blamed Iran for stepping up attacks on vessels. Traders add a risk premium to prices when supply routes look unsafe.
A hurricane added to the pressure by forcing producers to shut in about 500,000 barrels a day in the US Gulf of Mexico, around 25% of production there. Prices then pulled back from their session highs after President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections.
Oil is a cost for almost every business, so lasting higher prices can lift inflation across the economy.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil prices jump after tanker attacks near a key shipping route
levels.body:
Oil prices jumped on 8 October because ships carrying oil were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz. It was a record number of attacks. The main international price, Brent crude, rose 4% to $104.28 a barrel.
The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow stretch of sea between Iran and Oman. A lot of the world's oil travels through it. Fewer ships are now crossing, and the number is at its lowest for two months. Reports blamed Iran for stepping up the attacks.
A hurricane also hit oil production in the Gulf of Mexico, where companies stopped about 500,000 barrels a day. That is about a quarter of the production there. Prices fell back a little after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections.
When oil costs more, petrol, diesel and the cost of moving goods can all go up, and that can make everyday things dearer.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil gets dearer as ships are attacked near a key sea route
levels.body:
Oil prices rose on 8 October after a record number of attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude, the main international price, went up 4% to $104.28 a barrel.
The strait is a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that a big share of the world's oil passes through. Fewer ships are crossing, at a two-month low. Reports blamed Iran for stepping up the attacks, and when supply looks at risk, buyers pay more.
A hurricane also stopped about 500,000 barrels a day in the US Gulf of Mexico, around 25% of production there. Prices eased after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections.
Dearer oil can lift the cost of petrol, diesel and transport, and so push up prices in the shops.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil gets more expensive after attacks on ships near a key sea route
levels.body:
The price of oil went up on 8 October after more ships carrying oil were attacked than ever before near the Strait of Hormuz. The main world price, called Brent crude, rose by 4% to $104.28 a barrel.
The strait is a narrow stretch of sea between Iran and Oman. A big share of the world's oil is sent by ship through it. Fewer ships are going through now, the lowest number in two months. News reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks.
Oil also faced a problem in the United States. A hurricane meant companies stopped pumping about 500,000 barrels a day in the Gulf of Mexico, around a quarter of what the area normally produces. The price dipped after President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the elections in November.
If oil stays expensive, it can push up the cost of fuel and of moving goods, and so the price of many things in shops.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil prices rise because ships have been attacked
levels.body:
The price of oil went up on 8 October. Ships carrying oil were attacked near a narrow stretch of sea called the Strait of Hormuz. There were more attacks than ever before. The main price, called Brent, went up 4% to $104.28 for a barrel.
The strait lies between Iran and Oman. Lots of the world's oil goes through it by ship. Now fewer ships are going through. News reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks. When oil might be harder to get, buyers pay more.
A storm also hurt oil making in the United States. Firms stopped about 500,000 barrels a day in the Gulf of Mexico. That is about a quarter of the oil made there. The price fell a little when President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November elections.
Dearer oil can make petrol and transport cost more, and that can make shop prices rise.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil costs more after ships are attacked at sea
levels.body:
Oil got more expensive on 8 October. Ships that carry oil were attacked near a narrow sea route called the Strait of Hormuz. It was the most attacks ever counted. A barrel of the main kind of oil, called Brent, cost $104.28 at the end of the day. That was 4% more than before.
Oil is the thick liquid that is turned into petrol and diesel. A lot of it travels by ship through the strait, which lies between Iran and Oman. Fewer ships are going through now. News reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks. If supply may be short, people pay more.
A big storm made things worse. It stopped about a quarter of the oil being pumped in the Gulf of Mexico. The price fell back a little when US President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran before elections in November.
If petrol and transport cost more, things in shops can cost more too.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil costs more because ships have been attacked
levels.body:
The price of oil went up on 8 October. Some ships that carry oil were attacked at sea. This is the most attacks ever counted. The attacks were near a narrow sea route called the Strait of Hormuz. A barrel of oil cost $104.28 at the end of the day.
Oil is used to make petrol for cars. Lots of it goes on big ships through that sea route. Now fewer ships are going. News reports said the country of Iran was behind more of the attacks. When oil is harder to get, it costs more, like when a toy is hard to find in the shops.
A big storm also stopped some oil being pumped in the United States. The price dropped a little when the US leader, President Trump, said the US would not attack Iran before elections in November.
This matters because when oil costs more, petrol and the things that are driven to shops can cost more too.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

levels.headline: Why oil got more expensive
levels.body:
Imagine a lot of the fuel for the whole world has to travel along one small road. Last week, trucks on that road were attacked. Now fewer trucks go, and fuel costs more. That is what happened with oil on 8 October.
The small road is a narrow bit of sea called the Strait of Hormuz. Ships carry oil through it. There were more attacks on the ships than ever. Fewer ships are going now. A barrel of oil cost $104.28, which is 4% more than before.
A storm also stopped some of the oil being pumped in America. The price went down a little when President Trump said America would not attack Iran before the elections in November.
When oil costs more, it can cost more to drive cars and to bring food to the shops. Grown-ups pay close attention to that.
levels.why: Higher oil prices can raise fuel, transport and shop prices.

headline: Trump says US will not attack Iran before November midterm elections

terms.meaning: US elections held halfway through a president's term to choose members of Congress.

levels.headline: Trump says US will not attack Iran before November midterm elections
levels.body:
President Donald Trump said on Thursday 8 October that the United States would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections. The remark came as oil prices climbed on a record number of tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, and it helped prices come off their session highs.
Reports have blamed Iran for stepping up attacks on tankers in the area. The midterms are the elections held halfway through a US presidential term, in which voters choose all of the House of Representatives and part of the Senate.
The statement does not settle the tensions around the strait, and oil traders were also watching the impact of a hurricane on US Gulf production.
It matters because a possible military clash with Iran would raise risks for shipping, energy prices and the wider world economy.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: Trump rules out attack on Iran until after the midterms
levels.body:
President Donald Trump said on 8 October that the United States would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections. Oil prices, which had jumped on a record number of tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, eased from their highs after his comment.
Reports blamed Iran for stepping up attacks on ships. The midterms are held halfway through a presidential term, when Americans vote for the whole House of Representatives and a share of the Senate.
The comment leaves open what happens after the vote, and tensions around the strait remain, with traders also watching a hurricane that hit US Gulf production.
Any clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: Trump says no US strike on Iran before November
levels.body:
President Donald Trump said on 8 October that the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections in November. Oil prices had risen sharply after a record number of tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz and came off their highs after the remark.
Reports blamed Iran for stepping up the attacks. The midterms take place halfway through a president's term and decide who controls Congress.
The pledge covers only the period before the vote. Tensions in the area remain, and markets were also watching a hurricane's effect on US Gulf oil output.
A military clash could threaten shipping lanes and push up energy costs around the world.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: Trump says the US will not attack Iran before November
levels.body:
US President Donald Trump said on 8 October that the United States would not attack Iran before the midterm elections in November. Oil prices had jumped because of a record number of attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. They fell back from their highest levels after he spoke.
News reports blamed Iran for stepping up the attacks. The midterms are elections held halfway through a president's four-year term. They decide who controls Congress, the part of the US government that makes laws.
His words only cover the time until the vote. Worries remain about the shipping route, and traders were also watching a hurricane that hit oil production in the US.
A fight with Iran could make shipping unsafe and push up the price of fuel around the world.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: Trump says no US attack on Iran before the midterm elections
levels.body:
President Donald Trump said on 8 October that the United States would not attack Iran before the midterm elections in November. Oil prices had jumped on a record number of tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, and they eased after his comment.
Reports blamed Iran for stepping up the attacks. The midterms are elections held halfway through a president's term, when voters choose who sits in Congress, the part of government that makes US laws.
The comment covers only the time before the vote, so worries about shipping remain. Traders were also watching a hurricane that hit oil production in the US Gulf.
A clash with Iran could make shipping unsafe and push fuel prices up around the world.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: Trump says America will not attack Iran before the elections
levels.body:
President Donald Trump of the United States said on 8 October that his country would not attack Iran before elections in November. On the same day, oil had become more expensive because of a record number of attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz. After he spoke, the oil price fell back a little.
Reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks. The November elections are called the midterms. They take place halfway through a president's time in office, and they decide who controls Congress, the group that makes the country's laws.
He only talked about the time before the vote. People are still worried about ships at sea, and a hurricane has also hurt oil making in the US.
A fight with Iran could make oil much dearer for people everywhere.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: The US leader says no attack on Iran for now
levels.body:
The leader of the United States, President Donald Trump, said on 8 October that his country would not attack Iran before elections in November. That day, oil had become dearer because ships had been attacked near the Strait of Hormuz. The price dropped a little after he spoke.
News reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks. The November elections are called the midterms. They happen halfway through a president's time in the job. People vote for who will sit in Congress, the group that makes laws in the US.
He only talked about the time until the vote. People are still worried about the ships. A storm also hurt oil making in the US.
If there was a fight, oil could get much dearer, and that would affect people far away.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: A promise about a possible fight
levels.body:
The leader of the United States, President Donald Trump, said that his country would not attack another country, Iran, before big elections in November. Elections are when people vote to choose who will make decisions. He said this on 8 October.
Why did people care? Ships carrying oil had been attacked near a narrow stretch of sea, and news reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks. Oil had become dearer. After he spoke, the price fell back a little.
He only promised for the time until the vote. People are still worried about the ships.
If countries fight, ships can be unsafe and oil can cost much more everywhere.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: A promise from the leader of America
levels.body:
The leader of America, President Trump, made a promise on 8 October. He said America would not attack the country of Iran until after some big votes in November. A vote is when people choose who will lead them.
Many people were listening. Ships that carry oil had been attacked near a narrow sea route. News reports said Iran was behind more of the attacks. Oil had become dearer. After the promise, the price came down a little, like when everyone calms down after a shout.
The promise only lasts until the votes.
If countries argue and fight, many people can be affected, even far away.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.

levels.headline: When leaders promise not to fight
levels.body:
Sometimes leaders of countries argue, a bit like children in a playground. The leader of America, President Trump, said on 8 October that America would not start a fight with Iran until after some big votes in November.
People listened closely. Some ships carrying oil had been attacked at sea, and oil had become dearer. When he made his promise, the price came down a little. It was like a teacher saying 'let's all calm down'.
The promise only lasts until the votes. Grown-ups are still worried about the ships.
When countries fight, many people can be affected, even those far away.
levels.why: A clash with Iran could disrupt shipping and raise energy prices worldwide.
